title: route step config
description: Resolves a label for the input with a classifier, embedding similarity, a prior LLM verdict or a prior decision, and jumps to the first rule whose label matches.

model_id.description: Logical id of the classifier or embedding model; required for the classifier and embedding_knn strategies, unused by llm_structured and decision.

strategy.description: How the label is resolved: the classifier's top label, the nearest reference embedding, a prior LLM verdict matched against rule labels, or a prior decide choice.

input_field.description: Context key holding the text to route on; required for the decision strategy, where it is <decide step>.<question>.

min_confidence.description: Decision strategy only: a choice whose <input_field>.confidence is below this takes default_step, which it requires; 0 turns the check off.

default_step.description: Step taken when no rule matches; when unset the pipeline ends.

labels.description: Classifier strategy only: labels to classify against, sent with every call in place of the model's own: names, or objects with a name and a description. Every rule label must be one of them. Needs a zero-shot model (gliner_classifier, gliner_ner, or a decision model published as a classifier); any other model fails the pipeline load. Unset, the model's own labels apply.

rules.description: Ordered rules; the first one whose label equals the resolved label wins.

items.description: One routing rule: a label, the step taken when it wins and, for embedding_knn, the reference sentences.

label.description: Label to match; one of labels when the step sets them; for embedding_knn without sentences it is also the reference text.

next_step.description: Id of the step taken when this rule matches.

sentences.description: embedding_knn only: reference sentences embedded for this rule; the label is used when none are given.

label.description: A label name, or an object with the name and a description.

name.description: The label, as the step's results, rules and triggers name it.

description.description: What the label means; the model reads it, so a precise sentence classifies better than a bare word.
